objectives: I can open a conversation in English using an appropriate phrase.
I can keep a conversation going by showing interest or asking for clarification.
I can close a conversation politely in English.

stages.name: Opening: Retrieval, Bridge, I can...
stages.purpose: Activate prior knowledge of school vocabulary and simple present, connect it to today's speaking focus, and state the learning intention.

procedure.text: Quick-fire retrieval (whole class, oral): 1) Name 5 school subjects in English -- pairs have 30 seconds. 2) Complete: 'I ___ (go) to school every day. She ___ (have) Maths on Tuesday.' 3) True or false: 'In German you say Ich gehe -- in English you also say I go, not I go-e.' 4) Give me one phrase you already know for starting a conversation in English.
Teacher reveals answers on board. For item 4, take 2-3 responses. Write them up -- pupils will revisit after the input stage.
Bridge (spoken): 'In the last lesson you heard and saw phrases for starting and ending conversations. You recognised them. Today you use them -- your voice, your words. Same phrases, new challenge.'
Write on board and read aloud: 'I can open, continue, and close a short conversation in English about school topics.' Leave visible for the whole lesson.

stages.name: Input and Modelling
stages.purpose: Introduce the five target conversation phrase types through live demonstration and explicit reference so pupils have a clear model before they practice.

procedure.text: Display the conversation phrases reference on screen. Read through each phrase type aloud (opener informal, opener formal, continuer -- interest, continuer -- clarification, closer). Pupils listen only.
Live demo: do a short conversation with one pupil volunteer (or read both parts aloud if no volunteer). Pause after each phrase and say which type it is: 'That was a continuer -- I showed interest.'
Pupils copy the five phrase types and one example each into their notebooks. Point out: 'handy' in English means useful or convenient -- NOT mobile phone.

stages.name: Guided Practice -- Band 1 (Supported)
stages.purpose: Build confidence and recognition by completing a school conversation with missing phrase words -- full support, one correct answer per blank.

procedure.text: Hand out (or display) the gap-fill exercise. Read the instruction aloud: 'Fill in each blank with the missing word. The hint tells you what kind of word to use. The first example is done for you.'
Partner swap and check, then teacher reveals answers. Ask: 'Which blank was hardest? Why?'

stages.name: Guided Practice -- Band 2 (Guided)
stages.purpose: Consolidate phrase recognition by matching full phrases to their conversational function -- phrases still on screen, but pupils must identify the function themselves.

procedure.text: Display (or hand out) the matching exercise. Remind pupils: the phrase list from the grammar reference is still on screen as support. The task is to identify what each phrase does.
Pupils complete the matching exercise individually.
Pairs compare, then whole-class check. For any disagreement: 'What made you think that phrase was a continuer rather than a closer?' Elicit reasoning.

stages.name: Independent Production -- Band 3 (Free speaking)
stages.purpose: Push pupils to produce the target phrases in genuine spoken interaction -- no frames, no word bank, only a situation prompt.

procedure.text: Remove (or minimise) the phrase display. Hand out one situation card per pair. Read the task aloud: 'Have a real conversation. Use one opener, at least one continuer, and one closer. You have the card -- everything else comes from you.'

Pairs have their conversation using the situation card. Teacher circulates quietly and notes on a piece of paper: one strong phrase use per pair (for sharing in wrap-up) and one error pattern to address (for next lesson).
Signal end. Brief pause before wrap-up.

stages.name: Wrap-up
stages.purpose: Consolidate today's phrases through shared production and a written exit check that confirms individual recall.

procedure.text: Invite 2-3 pairs to share one exchange from their conversation. After each, class identifies which phrase types they heard. Write strong examples on the board.
Exit slip (on paper or in notebook): 'Write one opener, one continuer, and one closer from today. Your own words -- no copying from the board.'
Preview: 'Next lesson -- same conversations, but we add something new: describing what happens at school from a different angle. We call it the passive voice.'

differentiationNotes: Weaker pupils: phrase reference stays visible during Band 2 and Band 3. Reduce Band 3 situation card to one task only (e.g. 'find out what they did in summer'). Pair with a stronger speaker. Stronger pupils: Band 3 -- must use all five phrase functions (opener, two different continuers, one clarification, closer) and may not repeat any phrase used in Bands 1 or 2. Early finishers: swap cards and repeat with a new situation.
exercisePlan: gap_fill: School conversation -- fill in the phrases (Band 1) -- 5 items, missing key words from conversation openers/continuers/closers, full hint per blank
matching: Conversation phrases -- match phrase to function (Band 2) -- 5 pairs, full phrases matched to opener/continuer/closer labels
